## Overview

The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) publishes [Country Report](../document-types/country-report.qmd)s every spring as part of the European Semester for each euro-area member state. These documents analyze economic, social, and fiscal developments, as well as the implementation of earlier recommendations. The current card draws on twenty-one documents covering [Austria](../countries/austria.qmd), [Belgium](../countries/belgium.qmd), [Bulgaria](../countries/bulgaria.qmd), [Croatia](../countries/croatia.qmd), [Cyprus](../countries/cyprus.qmd), [Estonia](../countries/estonia.qmd), [Finland](../countries/finland.qmd), [France](../countries/france.qmd), [Germany](../countries/germany.qmd), [Greece](../countries/greece.qmd), [Ireland](../countries/ireland.qmd), [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd), [Latvia](../countries/latvia.qmd), [Lithuania](../countries/lithuania.qmd), [Luxembourg](../countries/luxembourg.qmd), [Malta](../countries/malta.qmd), [Netherlands](../countries/netherlands.qmd), [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd), [Slovakia](../countries/slovakia.qmd), [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd), [Spain](../countries/spain.qmd), and [Croatia](../countries/croatia.qmd), all published in June 2026.

## Use in the Rating Process

The [Country Report](../document-types/country-report.qmd) feeds the discretionary adjustments process (DAP) by providing detailed qualitative and quantitative assessments for key parameters. It informs the assessment of [Growth](../parameters/growth.qmd) and competitiveness (C1*), the [Inflation Differential](../parameters/inflation-differential.qmd) (C2*), the [Fiscal Capacity](../parameters/fiscal-capacity.qmd) and medium-term fiscal plan (C3*), [Refinancing Need](../parameters/refinancing-need.qmd) and debt sustainability (R1*), the [Backstop Eligibility](../parameters/backstop-eligibility.qmd) context (R6*), the banking sector (C5*), and [Outlook Factors](../parameters/outlook-factors.qmd) such as geopolitical risks and structural vulnerabilities (R7*).

## Methods

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) uses historical data and medium-term forecasts (e.g., Spring 2026 Forecast) to assess [Growth](../parameters/growth.qmd), noting productivity trends and GDP drivers. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 11, p. 58" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 11, p. 58">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal [Fiscal Capacity](../parameters/fiscal-capacity.qmd) is assessed based on the general government balance, primary balance, and structural adjustments, referencing specific forecast years. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 42" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 42">ⓘ</button>
- [Refinancing Need](../parameters/refinancing-need.qmd) and debt sustainability are evaluated using debt-to-GDP ratios and public investment levels, within the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s debt sustainability analysis framework. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 42" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 42">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports real GDP growth, nominal unit labour cost growth, and wage growth to assess economic momentum and competitiveness pressures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- [Inflation Differential](../parameters/inflation-differential.qmd) is assessed using Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) data to evaluate price stability and differentials. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal capacity evaluations include tax revenue structures and spending compositions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 15" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 15">ⓘ</button>
- Refinancing risks are analyzed via tax arrears and shadow economy estimates. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 15" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 15">ⓘ</button>
- [Backstop Eligibility](../parameters/backstop-eligibility.qmd) context is derived from compliance with EU fiscal frameworks and the use of flexibility clauses. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6">ⓘ</button>
- [Outlook Factors](../parameters/outlook-factors.qmd) are assessed through structural issues like public procurement inefficiencies and institutional quality. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 11, p. 14, p. 17, p. 80" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 11, p. 14, p. 17, p. 80">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) estimates potential growth using production function approaches, accounting for labour supply and total factor productivity. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal capacity is monitored via the medium-term fiscal-structural plan and excessive deficit procedures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 37" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 37">ⓘ</button>
- The report uses historical GDP growth data and medium-term forecasts to assess growth potential, highlighting structural factors such as labor market rigidity and low business dynamism as constraints on productivity and growth. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 9-10" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 9-10">ⓘ</button>
- The document analyzes fiscal capacity through the lens of the medium-term fiscal structural plan, assessing the plausibility of the projected primary balance improvements. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The report details the composition of public debt and financing needs, including the impact of high interest payments and the use of EU loans for defence. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 29" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- The assessment of backstop eligibility is informed by Belgium’s status under the Excessive Deficit Procedure and its compliance record. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 24" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 24">ⓘ</button>
- The document relies on the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) Spring 2026 Forecast for projections of the general government deficit and debt, assessing fiscal capacity through the new national fiscal framework. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The assessment of backstop eligibility is informed by the status of the excessive deficit procedure, noting it is held in abeyance due to the national escape clause. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 27" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 27">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)’s medium-term growth forecasts deviate from historical means, influenced by structural factors such as demographic trends, energy prices, and sectoral shifts. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission’s debt sustainability analysis indicates high fiscal sustainability risks in the medium term for France. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The MRP inputs for refinancing need are derived from the projected general government debt stock, interest expenditure, and primary balance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The assessment considers France’s status under the EU fiscal framework (EDP) and compliance with recommendations. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses the Commission Spring 2026 Forecast to project potential growth and real GDP growth. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal projections are based on the medium-term fiscal-structural plan and the Commission Spring 2026 Forecast. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 7, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 7, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- Debt and deficit figures are sourced from the Commission Spring 2026 Forecast and national accounts. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses historical gross domestic product growth data and medium-term forecasts to assess the growth trend. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 2-3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 2-3">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports the general government balance and primary surplus as percentages of gross domestic product. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 5-6, p. 36-37" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 5-6, p. 36-37">ⓘ</button>
- The document provides general government gross debt as a percentage of gross domestic product, with projections for 2026 and 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 38-39, p. 61-62" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 38-39, p. 61-62">ⓘ</button>
- The document references [Greece](../countries/greece.qmd)’s status under the Stability and Growth Pact, including the activation of the National Escape Clause. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 32, p. 36" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 32, p. 36">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses historical GDP growth data to illustrate productivity stagnation and regional disparities. It references Eurostat and [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) forecast data for medium-term trends. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 47" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 47">ⓘ</button>
- The report relies on the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) Spring 2026 Forecast for deficit and debt projections. It analyzes the primary balance and the impact of stock-flow adjustments. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 47" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 47">ⓘ</button>
- The document details the debt stock, including holdings by insurers and pension funds, and discusses the cost of servicing public debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 76" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 76">ⓘ</button>

- The document reports HICP inflation forecasts for 2026 and 2027. It does not provide a specific euro-area average inflation projection for direct differential calculation, but implies convergence toward the ECB target via the 2027 forecast of 2.2%. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports primary balance proxies via general government deficit and debt ratios. It details the impact of defence spending and tax reforms on fiscal sustainability. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports general government debt-to-GDP ratios and gross financing needs are implicit in the deficit and debt figures. It notes the activation of the national escape clause. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The European Commission uses standard national accounts data for GDP. It also references Modified Gross National Income (GNI*) to better reflect the income standards of Irish residents, excluding globalization effects. The report notes that GDP figures are heavily influenced by multinational activity. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The European Commission assesses fiscal position using both standard GDP-based metrics and GNI*-adjusted metrics. It highlights the distortion caused by windfall corporate taxes in headline budget figures. The primary balance is implied by the general government surplus given the low debt stock. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 31" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- Debt sustainability analysis is based on the Commission’s Spring 2026 Forecast. The report notes significant stock-flow adjustments affecting the debt trajectory. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 31" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) estimates real GDP growth based on contributions from private consumption, investment, and net exports. Potential growth is linked to productivity shifts towards higher value-added activities. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>, <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 10" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 10">ⓘ</button>
- HICP inflation projections account for rising fuel and service prices, linked to geopolitical conflicts (Middle East) and domestic demand. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal projections incorporate the national escape clause for defence spending and tax reforms. The primary balance is implied by the general government balance and interest expenditure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>, <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 39" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- Refinancing needs are influenced by rising public debt and defence spending. Domestic bank lending and capital market depth are key constraints on financing behaviour. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 61" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 61">ⓘ</button>, <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 66" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 66">ⓘ</button>
- The document provides estimates for real GDP growth, nominal growth components (private and government consumption, net exports, investment), and detailed analysis of productivity trends using unit labor costs and total factor productivity. - Debt stock and composition are discussed in Annex 2, referencing general government debt-to-GDP ratios and projections. - The report provides historical real GDP growth and medium-term forecasts based on the European Commission's Spring 2026 Forecast. - The document provides data on general government balance, structural primary balance, and debt-to-GDP ratios, which are critical for assessing fiscal capacity and debt sustainability. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4, 35" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4, 35">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports gross general government debt levels. - The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) estimates potential growth and historical trends using standard macroeconomic models, noting structural constraints such as labor productivity gaps and aging demographics. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 3, 50-51" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 3, 50-51">ⓘ</button>

- The analysis focuses on the best five-year average primary balance and current-year projected primary balance. The document highlights the need for significant fiscal consolidation to meet EU targets, noting the absence of a comprehensive long-term fiscal strategy. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 4, 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 4, 5">ⓘ</button>
- The report addresses the current account deficit and government debt dynamics, noting the persistent deficits and rising debt levels. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3, 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3, 5">ⓘ</button>
- Structural factors such as regional disparities, low innovation, energy dependency, and weaknesses in the justice and anti-corruption systems are highlighted as key outlook factors. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3, 4, 10, 18" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3, 4, 10, 18">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses European Commission Spring 2026 Forecast data for GDP growth projections. It highlights structural productivity challenges rather than short-term volatility. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal assessments are based on the general government deficit and debt-to-GDP ratios, along with the medium-term fiscal structural plan (MTFSP). The primary balance target of 1.6% of GDP is derived from the MTFSP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 35" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- Debt sustainability is assessed through the evolution of the debt-to-GDP ratio, public investment levels, and stock-flow adjustments. The document does not provide explicit gross financing need figures but implies manageable refinancing conditions given the declining debt ratio and ECB support. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 35" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- The document extensively discusses structural reforms, political fragmentation, and regional disparities as key drivers of future economic performance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 7" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 7">ⓘ</button>
